ut_ogden.blurb: Ogden sits in the northern Wasatch, with crags close enough to town to climb after work. Trad, sport and bouldering are in roughly even balance, with a little ice and mixed. The rock is mostly quartzite, with some limestone and conglomerate in the mix. Roped grades cluster from 5.8 to 5.12, peaking at 5.10 and 5.11, and the boulder problems cover mostly the easier V grades with a tail of hard ones. The Schoolroom is a stack of tiered cliff bands above the east side of the city, with sport lines from 5.6 to 5.13. The Mezzanines are trad cliffs west of Lewis Peak, and the Ogden Boulder Field fills the foothills with problems. Winter makes outdoor climbing hard. Waterfall Canyon holds an ice route.

co_west_of_rustic.blurb: West of Rustic is the stretch of Poudre Canyon beyond Rustic near Fort Collins, where the valley opens wide and fills with cliffs and boulders. It is the strongest bouldering in the Fort Collins area, and boulder problems outnumber everything else by a wide margin, with sport climbing a clear second and a thin trad presence. Problems spread across the whole V scale, with plenty in the middle grades and a good number of hard ones. Sport routes mostly run 5.10 to 5.13. Rock in the canyon as a whole is granite, gneiss and schist, and quality ranges from solid to loose. Poudre Falls is mainly a sport crag, and Boston Peak is another sport spot.

id_north_idaho.blurb: North Idaho covers the northern panhandle, with climbing spread around Coeur d'Alene, Sandpoint, Bonners Ferry and Moscow. Sport, bouldering and trad are close to evenly matched, with a small alpine and ice side. Most roped climbs are 5.8 to 5.11, with the bulk at 5.10, so it suits climbers who want moderate cragging more than hard projects. Boulder problems are mostly V0 to V5. Q'Emiln Park, on the Spokane River in Post Falls, is the biggest single area, a 78-acre park with more than a hundred routes where the climbing mostly stays at 5.10 and below. The Selkirk Crest is where the trad and alpine routes concentrate, while Tubbs Hill adds boulders.

co_main_canyon_unaweep_granite.blurb: Unaweep Canyon, near Grand Junction along Highway 141, is a pocket of granite and gneiss surrounded by sandstone country. Trad climbing is the core, led by crack climbing, with a smaller group of bolted routes. Most climbs are 5.8 to 5.12, with the bulk at 5.10 and 5.11. Cliffs range from roughly 150 to over 900 feet. The rock is complex, so solid stretches can turn blocky and loose. Spring and fall are the best seasons, though sun and shade can be chased all year: the north side of the road warms in cooler months, while the south side shades in summer. Mother's Buttress offers cracks from 5.7 to 5.10 along with face lines, Quarry Wall has among the highest concentrations of cracks, and Mighty Mouse Wall is face climbing.

oh_southeast_ohio.blurb: Southeast Ohio is hill country built around sandstone, with cliff bands and plenty of standalone boulders, and Athens and Marietta serve as the main hubs. Bouldering dominates, with smaller numbers of sport, trad and top-rope routes. Roped grades mostly fall between 5.5 and 5.10, and problems run mainly from V0 to V4. Rock quality swings widely, from very hard sandstone to crumbly stone, so it pays to judge each spot as you find it. Wayne National Forest and the Athens area hold most of the bouldering. Hocking Hills State Forest has nearly a mile of cliff with cracks, overhangs and flat faces, and Kiedaisch Point mixes trad and sport. Most areas sit down country roads, so the driving can be as much of an adventure as the climbing.

ma_greater_lynn_woods_area.blurb: Lynn Woods is a 2,200-acre municipal forest about ten miles north of Boston, and it is described as the largest climbing area in New England. It is nearly all bouldering, with a handful of roped routes. Hundreds of glacial erratics are scattered through quiet woods, offering over a thousand problems up to about 20 feet. Grades run from V0 into the double digits, with most between V1 and V6. The rock is coarse granite with plenty of grip, though long sessions can wear down your skin. Expect technical slabs, crimpy faces, steep overhangs and powerful lines. Walks range from a few steps to about half an hour. The Promised Land is the largest cluster, followed by Ridge Boulders and Wasteland Boulders.
